title: Search Smarter, Not Harder: A Scalable, High-Quality Zoned Neutral Atom Compiler
evidence_span: The compiler introduces Iterative Diving Search to avoid the memory demands of prior methods and relaxed routing to reduce atom rearrangement; evaluation compiles circuits with thousands of qubits and reports 28.1% average lower rearrangement overhead.
problem: Zoned neutral-atom architectures may scale to thousands of qubits, but existing compilers require excessive memory and fail to scale beyond small circuits.
method_or_artifact: Goal-directed Iterative Diving Search compiler and relaxed atom-routing optimization.
workload_or_benchmark: Quantum circuits with thousands of qubits on zoned neutral-atom architectures; circuit suite, qubit counts, runtime, and compilation-quality metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Zoned neutral-atom quantum computer with atom rearrangement and routing operations; trap geometry, movement timing, and gate model are unspecified.
limits: The description omits circuit suite, memory footprint, compilation time, fidelity, routing constraints, and baseline configurations.
Rearrangement overhead reduction may trade off circuit depth, fidelity, or search optimality.
Official description only; compiler scalability and quantum-system validity require paper-level verification.

title: Janus: Compiler-Based Defense Against Transient Execution Attacks Using ARM Hardware Primitives
evidence_span: Janus integrates speculative-execution and control-flow dependencies with ARM pointer-authentication modifiers and BTI features, using modifier fusion and protected-variable carrier reuse to reduce overhead; on SPEC CPU2017 it reports 3.85% average overhead and 2.97–7.80% overhead on real-world applications.
problem: Transient execution attacks such as Spectre and control-flow hijacking require defenses that protect speculation without imposing large performance or code-size costs.
method_or_artifact: Compiler-based defense using ARM pointer authentication and BTI primitives, modifier fusion, and carrier-register reuse.
workload_or_benchmark: SPEC CPU2017 and real-world ARM64 applications; compiler version, attack variants, optimization settings, and security coverage are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: ARM64 processors with pointer-authentication and BTI microarchitectural features; hardware generation, OS, ABI, and attacker model are unspecified.
limits: The description omits attack coverage, code-size effects, security proof, hardware/OS versions, and baseline defenses.
Low average overhead does not establish protection against all transient-execution variants.
Official description only; security and performance claims require paper-level verification.

title: Seeing Through Silicon: Multimodal Thermal Reconstruction via Physics-Informed Diffusion
evidence_span: The framework fuses performance-counter heat-generation signals with sparse thermal sensors using a physics-informed conditional diffusion model constrained by the heat equation and explicit vertical coupling; the official description reports 0.48°C versus 13.08°C RMSE, over 94% lower estimation error, 0.95 s versus 147 s inference time, and R² above 0.99 against finite-element simulation.
problem: 3D-IC thermal fields are volumetric and poorly observable from either performance counters or sparse sensors alone, limiting real-time thermal management.
method_or_artifact: Multimodal conditional diffusion reconstruction constrained by heat-equation physics and inter-layer coupling.
workload_or_benchmark: 3D integrated-circuit thermal monitoring and finite-element reference fields; designs, sensor layouts, power traces, and reconstruction resolution are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 3D IC with vertical heat coupling, performance counters, and sparse on-chip sensors; package, materials, thermal boundary conditions, and FEM configuration are unspecified.
limits: The description omits sensor count/layout, design set, spatial resolution, FEM hardware, and error distribution.
High R² and speedup depend on reference simulation and observation conditions; sensor drift and unseen power maps are unresolved.
Official description only; thermal fidelity and closed-loop claims require paper-level verification.

title: CLUE-ECC: Low-Cost LPDDR6 Reliability Enhancement by Integrating System ECC with On-Die ECC
evidence_span: CLUE-ECC pools 16-bit on-die and system ECC parity to correct LPDDR6 symbol-level errors, avoiding the correction gap of 8-bit Reed–Solomon codes without the parity budget of 12-bit codes; the official description reports 33.3% on-die parity storage, 14.83% area savings, and 24.18% power savings at unchanged bandwidth impact versus conventional Reed–Solomon coding.
problem: LPDDR6’s 12-bit data beat mismatches common 8- or 16-bit Reed–Solomon symbols, creating a trade-off between correction capability and on-die parity budget.
method_or_artifact: Joint system/on-die ECC parity pooling for symbol-level correction under LPDDR6 data-beat constraints.
workload_or_benchmark: LPDDR6 memory reliability and error-correction evaluation; fault patterns, ECC configurations, controller implementation, and bandwidth model are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: LPDDR6 DRAM with on-die and system ECC, Reed–Solomon codes, and symbol-level faults; process, die organization, timing, and controller are unspecified.
limits: The description omits fault model, correction guarantee, area/power boundary, controller overhead, and LPDDR6 implementation details.
Parity pooling and unchanged bandwidth may rely on specific error patterns and protocol assumptions.
Official description only; reliability and standards-compatibility claims require paper-level verification.

title: LOHA: A Latency-Optimized CPU-Storage Hybrid Architecture for Billion-Scale Graph-Based Vector Similarity Search
evidence_span: LOHA decouples CPU graph traversal from product-quantization re-ranking, offloading re-ranking to an in-storage accelerator that exploits SSD parallelism, and pipelines both stages with speculative re-ranking; the official description reports up to 9.6x, 6.2x, and 4.0x throughput improvements over CPU, GPU, and in-storage architectures.
problem: Billion-scale graph ANNS incurs excessive SSD I/O and latency when traversal and re-ranking remain coupled in conventional CPU/GPU/storage systems.
method_or_artifact: CPU–storage hybrid architecture with CPU traversal, in-storage PQ re-ranking, SSD parallelism, and speculative pipelining.
workload_or_benchmark: Billion-scale product-quantization graph ANNS; dataset, recall target, SSD, FPGA/accelerator, query rate, and baseline configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: CPU plus SSD/in-storage accelerator with parallel flash access; storage interface, flash geometry, host system, and accelerator resources are unspecified.
limits: The description omits recall, dataset, SSD/accelerator configuration, I/O volume, latency, and baseline tuning.
Speculative re-ranking may trade extra reads, storage wear, and recall against throughput.
Official description only; hardware and workload claims require paper-level verification.
